newsitem.title: FRANCE: Experiments invited on space station.
newsitem.headline: Experiments invited on space station.

text.p: The European Space Agency (ESA) called on European researchers on Thursday to submit applications to place experiments in an international space station to be assembled over the next five years.

ESA is building the station together with the United States, Russia, Japan and Canada. The station's first element is to be placed on orbit in November with the rest going up over the next five years.
Work aboard the station, which will be on orbit for more than 10 years, will begin in 1999.
ESA invited experiments in biology, physics, space technology and earth-watching which would allow researchers to test technology and produce commercial applications.
It said scientists from ESA's 14 member countries could apply and researchers from other countries were welcome to team up with them.
